author: Riley Johnson
title: Mill Mountain Star in Roanoke won't shine tonight due to safety hazard - NewsBreak
text:
By Riley Johnson No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
ROANOKE, Va. ( WFXR ) – The Mill Mountain Star will not be illuminated this evening, Wednesday, September 10, due to damage identified during an inspection earlier today, according to the City of Roanoke.
Roanoke’s Facilities & Custodial Management Division, in coordination with a lighting contractor, completed an assessment. The city reports that it was discovered that several bulbs had become detached and could swing freely.
According to officials, this poses a significant electrical safety hazard, as the swinging bulbs could cause live electrical connections to come into contact with the metal frame of the Star. Due to this, the Star will not be operational this evening
Roanoke City says the lighting contractor and staff have secured the necessary parts and will return tomorrow with a larger lift capable of reaching the top of the Star. The team will complete repairs, install the required components, and re-secure all bulbs safely.
Barring any unforeseen complications, officials report the Star is anticipated to shine red, white, and blue in remembrance of September 11 on Thursday.
